speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My reply has always been that I wish I have the power to turn back time.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As much as I try to live a life without regrets, there will always be regrets, always a wish that we could have done things better, always a wish that we could have spent more time with our loved ones." Regret is truly an incurable ache.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I found myself thinking about this wish again a few months back because I wished I had more time with Yu Xuan and got to know her better.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I had just met her two days earlier at an event and was mesmerised by her beautiful voice and her big heart.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She had concerns about and suggestions on how we can improve the busking scene.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I told her that I will look into it and catch up with her another time to discuss this further.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Unfortunately, I never got the chance to meet her again, but a promise is a promise and I fully intend to keep this promise.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I also met with the National Arts Council (NAC) as well and learnt about the amazing work they do.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have never been involved in the arts scene before.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As someone with two left feet and who cannot sing, dance, draw or paint, and I can tell you that my little daughters do all the above much better than me, I found myself in love with arts after these meetings.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I met with people so passionate about what they do, so devoted and selfless.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We spoke for hours and they were bursting with ideas and suggestions on how we can make things better not just for themselves but for everyone.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Unfortunately, some still view buskers as beggars and, for some, busking is frowned upon.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is time to change this perception and recognise buskers as artistes and performers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is time to fulfill the wishes of the buskers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They became friends through music, with Tristan attending vocal lessons together with Joey and even taking lessons from Yu Xuan at one point.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They started busking together in 2016 just to try it out.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In their words, "We sing from our hearts.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: When we sing, we interpret the songs and share our meaning and feelings with the audience." They did face many difficulties and, in particular, Yu Xuan had to overcome many health constraints to continue to busk.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But through busking, she found meaning in life.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Despite problems with her eyesight, then her kidney, then a stubborn cough, which damaged her vocal cords, then her spine, then her hearing, she never gave up.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The ETC busk because they want to make people believe in music and comfort and surprise them with this unexpected outdoor encounter.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They shared with me how difficult it was for them to find a spot and, at times, they spent the night moving in taxis from one location to another with all their equipment.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This means that buskers can move within an area to find an available site more easily.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They also had an idea of an app that shows the buskers what sites are taken and what sites are available, so buskers can move to the locations that are not being occupied instead of travelling all the way there to find that it has been taken.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The app can also be made available to the public and they can see where performances are taking place and this will help promote the busking scene in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I can understand the complexity of managing such an app.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But I think it is an idea we should explore further.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I met this young man who recently graduated from Engineering and has been busking for the past three years.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In his own words and on his signboard when he busks, "I busk to make the world a better place".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Busking means the world to him and it gave him a platform to perform and express himself.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Through busking, he realised his love for performing on the streets and how every song he sings can make a big impact on a person's life.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For him, it is the most heart-warming feeling ever.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But Firdaus is concerned that the current limited busking sites will cause a problem.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Due to the limited space, chances are buskers will be performing close to one another and most of them will not be happy about it.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They may be arguments among the buskers about noise and "stealing" away the crowd.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Due to it being first-come-first-serve, some buskers come as early as 11.00 am to reserve the "best" spots and only start performing in the evening.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Firdaus is concerned that the busking community will turn competitive and lose respect for one another.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is done for Covent Garden in London, a world-renowned site for street performances.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There are scheduled time slots for each performance area.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Buskers who wish to play, put their names on a list and names are drawn to see who gets to choose the most desired time slots first.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Names are drawn and slots are chosen until either nobody wants the leftover spots or all have been chosen.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We can also be fairer and have more diversity of performances in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Not all buskers are singers and I met Jonathan who, together with Edwin, are known as The Annoying Brothers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They started busking five years ago to push the boundaries of how a circus show can be presented in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: He started mixing with bad company when his parents were going through divorce.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: He shared with me that, "I was lucky as I met someone who introduced circus arts to me, which kept me at bay.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If not, I would not have become who I am today and may have ended up in jail.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Because of that, circus arts became a huge passion of mine and I aspire to become a circus artist, with the aims of developing this artform in Singapore." He also shared that, "Busking also allows me to share my art with people who may not be able to afford shows in the theatre.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: When I busk, it allows them to be exposed to the arts and also pay how much they can afford or not pay at all and still enjoy the show.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Busking allows me to make the world a better place and sometimes change someone's mood from bad to good because of my show." One main issue he faces as a circus act busker is that he has way fewer locations that he can use.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Examples of circus acts are magicians, jugglers, acrobats and dance groups.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They require a huge amount of space due to the nature of their shows and to ensure public safety.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The issue of first come, first served also puts them at a huge disadvantage because many musicians or sidewalk performers come really early to perform and again "chope" the space.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: His kind of performances are usually only possible in the evenings.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One thing he hopes for is for specific sites for circus acts at specific times.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This will make it a little fairer and will allow for more diversity of performances.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is a beautiful collaboration among the people, public and private sectors and I am delighted to support this.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I will also walk the talk in terms of my support for busking.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This new association will work closely with my team to manage these new sites, ensure that it is well-run and look into any feedback and address any concerns from both buskers and residents.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They do enliven the streets of Singapore, providing wholesome entertainment, lifting up our spirits and lightening our moods.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Busking provides the colours in an otherwise grey concrete jungle.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Surely, such a simple but meaningful contribution to the arts is worthy of being treated as a "real job for those who go down that road less trodden?” Sir, one of the last songs that Yu Xuan sang was 海阔天空, a song alluding to one’s struggles to stay true to one’s ideals while facing the inevitable headwinds and storms in life.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I guess it was apt that this was one of the last songs that she sang and this is perhaps symbolic of the struggles she faced and the struggles buskers face.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Singapore and Singaporeans will miss her beautiful voice in our heartlands where she used to busk.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She will be remembered for sharing her love for music with everyone and for nurturing the next generation of buskers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She will be remembered for her passion for music, for never giving up and for her fighting spirit.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I hope we can make their wishes come true.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth agrees with Mr Louis Ng that busking adds vibrancy to our streets and public spaces and showcases the creative energy and talent of our performers to public audiences.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In managing the Busking Scheme, NAC stands guided by the priorities outlined in Our SG Arts Plan.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These include nurturing creative excellence, connecting communities through the arts, and presenting Singapore’s diverse arts and culture to as wide an audience as possible.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NAC is committed to working with its partners to improve the Busking Scheme and ensuring that it grows in a manner that benefits performers, venue owners and audiences alike.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Since its introduction in the 1990s, the Busking Scheme has undergone several enhancements due to feedback from members of the public, venue owners, buskers and Government agencies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For example, NAC has increased the frequency and capacity of busking auditions in response to growing interest over the years, especially from younger performers, who want to express their artistic interests.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This is more than double the number and proportion in 2008.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To cater to this demand, NAC has worked with venue owners to increase the number of designated busking locations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Notwithstanding these developments, we recognise that the utilisation of busking locations can be uneven and there is sometimes intense competition for locations deemed to have higher footfall and visibility.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NAC, therefore, welcomes suggestions from members of the community like Mr Louis Ng and our buskers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In this regard, I am delighted to learn that Mr Louis Ng has identified two new locations for busking in Yishun and invited interested parties like Timbre+ to pilot new busking models with him.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NAC will also take up Mr Louis Ng’s suggestion of using technology, like apps, to share information.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To help us ensure that the Busking Scheme succeeds, owners and managers of busking locations must also be on board.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: They must be comfortable opening their venues for busking and with the type of busking acts being performed, for example, circus acts, and also be confident that buskers will be respectful towards the space and the different members of the public who use it.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Busking that is congruent with the identity of the space will help to create value and thereby help busking flourish with strong public support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NAC is currently in discussion with some venue owners and managers to explore different models, including Mr Louis Ng’s suggestion for buskers to be allocated busking areas instead of sites.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This will shape the busking experience on their premises with them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For example, NAC is in discussion with Singapore River One, the venue manager for Singapore River, to explore ways to enhance the busking experience along Boat Quay, Clarke Quay and Robertson Quay in a holistic manner.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NAC is also working with *SCAPE, already a designated busking location in Orchard Road, to assess how current spaces can cater to a greater diversity of performances.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NAC and *SCAPE intend to test new ideas to better support the aspirations of our buskers today, especially youths, such as through performance spaces that showcase budding youth talents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This, along with other ideas, are currently being considered as we work together with youths to co-create a master plan to develop the Somerset Belt into a vibrant youth district that supports their aspirations and interests.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I encourage other venue owners and managers to contact NAC if they are similarly keen to re-imagine how busking can add to the vibrancy of their spaces.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: It is heartening that individuals who are passionate about busking have already decided to come together to take greater ownership of the busking scene in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Therefore, I welcome the initiative of Jonathon, Fadhil, Yong Kang, Benjamin, Firdaus and Marcus to register a Busking Association.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This seeks to encourage good busking etiquette among our buskers, as well as sensitivity to the different groups who use the public spaces where busking takes place.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Deputy Speaker, Mr Louis Ng spoke about the passing of Singapore artist and busker Yu Xuan in March this year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Those familiar with Xinyao would remember Yu Xuan, Joi Chua and Cai Li Lian’s rendition of the popular local composition “Friendship Forever” (细水长流).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Buskers like Yu Xuan add vibrancy to our public spaces when they showcase their talents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Moving forward, NAC will continue to work with various partners – buskers, venue owners and managers – to enhance the Busking Scheme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I strongly encourage the public to take note of and support our busking scene, so that it will continue to flourish for years to come, just like the song "Friendship Forever".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: (In English): In conclusion, I thank Mr Louis Ng for his suggestions, initiatives and commitment to bring busking to the next level.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We look forward to our continued partnership with him, the busking community and venue partners, as well as the support of the public, to achieve our shared vision for a vibrant and sustainable arts and culture scene in Singapore.
